note: Source of truth for the ladder epoch boundary the website labels weeks against. Read by scripts/weekly-league-manager.py (ladder_contract(), epoch_boundary()) and fetchable by pages. It lives in data, not in a script literal, because it has already moved twice in two days -- Pip, 2026-07-29: 'Let's keep using variables and not hardcoding things where we can!'. Nothing here may be edited to a value the game side has not published; see sources[].

board_key.note: The client sends the LADDER epoch, not the build version: GameConfig.get_board_version() returns "L" + LADDER_VERSION. Local board file leaderboard_<seed>__L3.json; remote POST body field version=L3; remote GET query version=L3. The build version never touches the board key again -- that is the whole point of the build-vs-ladder split, so a cosmetic patch bump can never again fork a board.

regularised_from.ladder_version_meaning: THE FRONTIER -- the ladder epoch a NEW week opens on. Read by weekly-league-manager.start_new_week() to stamp meta.ladder_version and the board key, and by check-blessing-consistency.py as this file's claim about the current epoch. It MOVES at every ladder fork. It is NOT the epoch an archived week ran under: that is resolved per-week by ladder_version_for() from epochs[].boundary_local, so a restamp can never relabel a closed epoch's weeks. See boundary_ladder_version.
regularised_from.boundary_ladder_version_meaning: HISTORICAL and fixed -- the ladder epoch in force at boundary_local, i.e. the epoch the regularisation cut itself was made on. Stamped into every weekly record as epoch.boundary_ladder_version; 44 archived records already carry 'L3'. This existed only implicitly until 2026-08-13, sharing the ladder_version field above, which meant moving the frontier L3 -> L4 would have silently rewritten all 44 of them.
regularised_from.boundary_rule: A league week is anomalous iff it STARTS before boundary_local. The boundary is the Hobart-midnight anchor of the first L3 week, NOT board_opens_local -- see boundary_why.
regularised_from.boundary_why: The unit being flagged is a whole league week (Fri 00:00 -> Thu 23:59:59 Australia/Hobart). Cutting at board_opens_local instead would put the boundary 17 hours inside the first L3 week, so that week would start before its own boundary and be flagged pre-L3 -- and a week half under L2 rules and half under L3 would be exactly the cross-epoch blend the ladder split exists to prevent. The board-open time is therefore recorded separately and stated on the page, so nothing claims the board was accepting scores from midnight.
regularised_from.board_opens_note: Approximate, from pdoom1: 'Fri ~1700: board opens', with the seed blessed at a ceremony ~1645 AEST the same day. Treat as approximate until the game side confirms.
regularised_from.seed_note: NO BLESSED SEED ON L4 YET, and this field must stay null until there is one. It was left reading weekly-2026-w31/blessed after the L3 -> L4 fork of 2026-08-07, which is a blessing of a CLOSED board (L3 closed with (weekly-2026-w31, L3); the capture is at public/leaderboard/data/preserved/2026-08-08-l3-epoch-close/). The seed the shipped client posts to is an OBSERVATION and lives in public/leaderboard/data/published-board.json, never here: this field is the machine mirror of a row in docs/LEAGUE_SEED_LEDGER.md, and the ledger has no L4 row. pdoom1 rolled the featured seed const to weekly-2026-w33 on 2026-08-13 (pdoom1#1214, e44660c4) ready for the Fri 2026-08-14 league, and that string is deliberately NOT copied here: scripts/test-weekly-league-boundary.py pins the invariant 'a seed is present IFF the status is blessed', because unblessed-with-a-seed is a value sitting where code reads it as canonical that nobody has blessed. FILLING THIS IS PIP'S, AFTER the Gate 5 ceremony and AFTER the ledger row -- a seat inferring a blessing is pdoom1-website#297.
regularised_from.reason_pre: Opened before the L2 -> L3 ladder fork. L3 removed the action-point pool entirely in favour of an attention economy, added office lease and lock-in, four-way founder hours, six previously-inert upgrades and a quirk rebalance. Scores set under the earlier rules are not comparable to scores set after them -- that non-comparability is the whole reason the ladder version is a separate key. Retained as a record of what the pipeline produced, NOT as a comparable competition result.
regularised_from.reason_post: Opened on or after the L2 -> L3 ladder fork, on a board keyed (seed, L<n>) where L<n> is this stamp's own ladder_version, by a rollover anchored to Friday 00:00 Australia/Hobart whose run-time -> week mapping is pinned by scripts/test-weekly-league-boundary.py. This sentence used to name L3 outright; it was stamped unchanged onto weeks that ran on L4.
regularised_from.seed_source: Blessed by Pip at [Gate 5] on 2026-08-21 and recorded in docs/LEAGUE_SEED_LEDGER.md (L5 row). Verified FROM THE ARTIFACT: v0.14.2 release_manifest.json, "league_seed": "weekly-2026-w33", "ladder_version": "5", commit_hash 38528c22. [Gate 6] was HELD 2026-08-21 while api.pdoom1.com was down, and was OPENED by Pip on 2026-08-24 once the host returned (re-measured: 208 board keys probed, 0 unreachable). THE BOARD IS OPEN. The sentence 'a blessed key is not an open board' stays, because it is the distinction this field exists to carry -- the two are tracked separately in epochs[].board_open, and this text asserted a stale hold for three days after its cause had ended.

epochs.note: v0.14.3 forked L5 -> L6 AND rolled the seed, moving both halves of the board key at once. That is why (weekly-2026-w33, L5) closed with ZERO entries: it was published for one afternoon, on a client v0.14.3 had already superseded, and no run ever reached it. Capture: public/leaderboard/data/preserved/2026-08-24-l5-epoch-close/. The release notes record the slip honestly -- the seed rolls to w34 (23 Aug) and w35 (24 Aug) were made in the repository and never reached a published build, so players stayed on w33/L5 until this release carried them across.

epochs.gate6: OPENED 2026-08-24 by Pip, in the website seat, three days after being HELD on 2026-08-21. The hold's stated cause -- api.pdoom1.com unreachable -- ended when the DreamCompute instance returned on 2026-08-21T22:22Z; re-measured 2026-08-24T00:27Z, 208 board keys probed, 0 unreachable, and independently re-checked against the live host the same morning. Nothing here inferred the opening: it is a ruling, recorded on the day it was given, and pdoom1-website#297 exists precisely to stop a seat writing this field without one.
epochs.board_open_note: board_open is the ONE field that says a player may score here and be shown. It is NOT implied by seed_status: a blessed key is a key nobody disputes; an open board is a board a human said may take scores. The two were conflated for three days in August 2026 and the gap is why the L5 board sat blessed-and-shut while real runs landed on a superseded epoch.
epochs.seed_evidence: Confirmed at ARTIFACT level, not from memory: the published v0.14.2 release_manifest.json carries "ladder_version": "5", "league_seed": "weekly-2026-w33" and "commit_hash": "38528c22cd7b3d282dc825fa03e941d43a7c87fe", which is the tagged commit. Cross-checked against the v0.14.2 git tag message and against godot/autoload/game_config.gd's FEATURED_SEED_OVERRIDE at that commit.
epochs.note: Blessed at [Gate 5] on 2026-08-21. The ladder forked L4 -> L5 because pdoom1 #1233 (doom-stream routing, closing a sink of up to -6 doom/turn) and #1230 (28 new events) both change what a score means on a given seed. The SEED IS HELD, not rolled: the epoch half moved, which forks the board key on its own. [Gate 6: BOARD OPENS] was HELD by the Commissioner on 2026-08-21 -- api.pdoom1.com was unreachable (ICMP, :22, :80 and :443 all TIMED OUT rather than refusing, so the host was down; not a token, which would need a server to read it and say no). Gate 5 checks 1-6 and 8 passed; check 7 (a named human attesting the live board) was UNAVAILABLE and was recorded as such rather than skipped. UPDATED 2026-08-24: the host returned 2026-08-21T22:22Z and [Gate 6] was OPENED by Pip on 2026-08-24 -- see board_open / board_opened_utc above. The sentence 'THE BOARD IS NOT OPEN' stood in this file for three days after its stated cause had ended, because the note recorded a measurement as though it were a standing fact. It is corrected here rather than deleted: the hold was real, and so was the lag.
